title: I built a Monster Tamer game that lets you scan real-world QR codes to breed and evolve infinite creatures. But is it worth it?
author: Savage_PrawnYT
selftext:
I spent a year building a system that turns QR codes into unique 3D monsters. I finally finished my first devlog explaining it a bit more. If you're a monster-tamer fan, I'd love to know if this looks too 'janky' or if the infinite variety and real breeding mechanics are worth it.

Game: World of Qreatures

Open World Monster Collector RPG

This project uses various AI tools as well as custom systems

More Info: 

**ARE THE QR CODE RESULTS RANDOM?**  
I designed this to be repeatable and consistent. Same qr code = same monster every time. Same parents = same child every time. The difference is you get to create new monster designs by basically merging the visuals and stats of any monsters. Repeatable consistent results , but each qr code is different.

**WHY BREED WHEN YOU CAN SCAN FOR INFINITE MONSTERS ANYWAY?**  
The point of the breeding is to give the player creative control and experiment. Breeding doesn’t give you just another random monster it actually looks like you merged two chosen monsters. If one monster had green wings there is a very good chance the child will have green wings but maybe the body of the other parent.

**WHAT OTHER FEATURES ARE IN THE GAME?**  
Lots of different new types , 28 in total, 18 classics plus 10 more including time, radioactive , plasma , quantum , and many more. New battle mechanics like irradiation , time rewind, quantum entanglement. PvP battles , wild monsters battles. 1v1 and 2v2, npc trainers and some that can choose monsters to counter what you have and scale with your current level. Trade monsters with friends. Explore the world to find rare abilities , powerful items, underwater exploration, deep cave systems, discover legendary monsters hidden in the open world, complete quests, this is only the start.

Wishlist now so you can play the free demo when it is ready! 

Full Trailer Here:   
[https://store.steampowered.com/app/4701360/World\_of\_Qreatures/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/4701360/World_of_Qreatures/)

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body: You made the entire game without prototyping the core loop? Pretty ballsy move

replies.author: Savage_PrawnYT
replies.body:
I'm not trying to sound sarcastic at all. I just genuinely am a bit confused by your question.

In my point of view, it's impossible to make any game without first starting with a prototype that you refine over time until you've completed it. It's impossible to iterate through the game development cycle without testing the core gameplay loop many times along the way.

To me, it feels like yes, I have started with a prototype, and yes, I have tested the gameplay loop. If you mean have I created a small vertical slice and then playtested it with a small, select audience to first prove the concept is fun, no, I haven't actually done that yet, but I am very confident in my idea. The core gameplay loop is very familiar to already well-known concepts like Pokémon, Temtem, and PalWorld. The difference is I am introducing new gameplay mechanics in battles, new element types and battle interactions, as well as the QR Code and breeding technology, which is done in a completely different way than I've ever seen done before.

On top of this, there are some other changes that I've always wanted to see in Monster Tamer games, like the amount of challenge you actually feel during play, meaningful exploration, and making an open world actually feel worth exploring.

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body:
Yeah that's what I mean, if your game depends on the fact that people must synch between phone and pc then to me that sounds like a huge hurdle for people to get past.
I don't own a steam deck but I suppose that you could lean into making it a gimmick to use it's camera, but even so I doubt most people will bring their steam deck out to hunt for QR codes, and while a phone is good for that you probably need a good bridge like being able to breed or trade monsters in the phone app as well. And then you should probably invest in infrastructure unless you don't care about cheating.
I don't doubt that your game is fun, it's the QR code mechanic for a PC game that seems risky.

replies.author: Savage_PrawnYT
replies.body:
Totally valid points I honestly really appreciate your feedback on this. You are spot on that the mobile app will be a portable hub to collect , scan, and breed monsters. The anti cheating thing is relatively simple as it will use server based verification for every monster. You can’t just hack local files and cheat in a cracked monster. 

But you are correct it is a barrier for some people. Some people will have a webcam on pc, some people will be happy to use mobile, and some players will be happy just playing the core game and might even get bored of scanning after a while. I will be releasing more wild monsters to catch in game every month. So even players who just to play the game without qr codes can still experience new monsters with zero effort.

It’s not perfect and it is a risk, but I’m just trying somthing new and seeing where it goes because this idea is what I am passionate about

replies.author: klas-klattermus
replies.body:
Server based verification requires reliable infrastructure, are you paying for that? Unless your game has in-game transactions the problem with infra is that it keeps costing regardless if your revenue keeps growing.
As for cheating, if it's all about sending a UID then have you safeguarded yourself from users submitting hacked values over a third party app? 


Well as long as the QR scanning isn't too integral to the experience then I guess the risk is mitigated.
I'm just being the devil's advocate, these kind of problems can be a pain in the ass

Plus hundreds more added over time with monthly updates. And the evolving and breeding of any of these monsters in unlimited combinations is all possible without needing a camera. replies.author: Savage_PrawnYT

This is a great question, actually I kind of encourage it , I think it would be cool to share monsters online. But that’s the thing. There are genuinely infinite monsters to find. And then infinitely more to evolve and breed into endless combinations. Some players will choose to look up powerful monsters posted by other players. And some will choose to not do this. And some will want to take the most powerful one they can find and just breed it to see what happens. 

For competitive battles, there will be modes for filtering out the most absolutely broken god tier monsters to keep battles balanced. Such as a base stat total cap (similar to how some games ban legendaries) But honestly I’ve generated thousands of monsters and I haven’t found a perfect stat monster yet but sure, it’s possible. So is winning the lottery.

And if I absolutely had to pick 1 thing that I think makes it special I’d choose the breeding not the QR codes. The real breeding system in this game uses layers of different Ai tools to actually take 2 monsters a player has as input and actually breed them to produce a new child species that has visual resemblance of both parents.  This, as far as I can tell, has never been done before in game. 

People who have commented here so far have not watched my gameplay trailer they have only seen a 12 second gif of scanning and breeding mechanics. Therefore they cannot possibly give  balanced advice as to what platform my game belongs on. Steam is where I will start my journey. I’d love to have my game be fully multi platform on consoles and mobile too. Perhaps I will get to that point one day. 

I value all of the feedback given and it genuinely helps me - especially by showing me how important communication and framing for my game. 

My plan is to make the game fun and balanced and enjoyable with emphasis on creativity and discovery. Some people will enjoy it and some people won’t. That is always the way things go. 

Scanning qr codes is a cool feature that allows for infinite new monsters to be created. But it’s the rest of the game (battles, quests , story, challenges, exploration, breeding, evolving) and how you use those monsters throughout the game that is the fun part.

I’ve learned everything on the go. Just to answer your worry about QR code safety. It’s actually simple in this case. Each qr code contains a string of letters or numbers (usually a website but not always). My system doesn’t open the link or save anything at all. It doesn’t care what the qr code is pointing to. It’s takes that string and hashes it into a random number. That number becomes the seed to a backend pipeline that creates the monster and send back to the game engine at runtime.

replies.author: Savage_PrawnYT
replies.body:
Thank you! So to answer your questions I am using unity 6 - URP. A year ago I had zero skills or experience in programming or even using blender and stuff. Never even opened unity before.

What I did was work very slowly to break down tasks into the tiniest step possible and get Ai to teach me things. Litterally screenshotting unity or blender and asking “what does this button do” . 

This went on and on for months. The biggest challenge is that I didn’t know what I didn’t know. So how could I learn it ?

I start with broad questions. “What are the top ten pillars of game dev that need careful consideration.” 

One of those might be Optimisation. 

So I dive deeper, and learn about tons of different elements to that. One of those elements is Occlusion Culling. So I dive deeper on that. I now understand lots about occlusion culling and ended up using a tool called Perfect Culling which is far better than unity’s own package. Then I give the Ai documentation for that tool and learn how to use it. 

For writing code yes the quick answer is vibe coding. But honestly it’s not that simple. You cannot just expect Ai to get complex things correct. I had to actually build one method at a time not even one script at a time. Every single method in every script gets the same multi step treatment. 

1. Discussion and planning. I refine what I want to make. What will the rules be.   
2. I ask for a first draft.  
3. I have the Ai explain every line to me so I understand exactly how it functions and what the costs are.  
4. I suggest changes  
5. I get another Ai to review and challenge it.   
6. I do a safety check - how will this new method effect my other scripts. Are there any improvements we can make to make sure the code is performant and robust.   
7. I don’t use automations I copy and paste snippets of code myself one at a time. With clear comments in my code so I can understand it.   
8. Test test test. 

I repeat this over and over thousands of times. Adding new features. Polishing old ones. I have used hundreds of millions of tokens. 

The misconception  is that a lot of people think vibe coding is just one shotting a crappy html flappy bird clone. 

I just see Ai as a tool to speed up my own learning. The faster I learn the better design choices I can make and the faster I can actually learn new more complicated stuff. 

Every mechanic, every design choice and architectural solution within a script and every idea has been my own. I am making my vision. I am just getting it to write for me and teach me the basics of how to use new tools. 

It’s hard work and you have to really want to learn. But yeah that’s how I have done it. Just talking with Gemini. Breaking things down. And moving very very slowly. That’s it. 

Sorry for the long reply but it’s dangerous to just say vibe coded without proper explanation as most people don’t understand the structure and planning behind every task. 

Happy to talk more about it if you want to know more!

comments.author: Savage_PrawnYT
comments.body:
BIG UPDATE:  
Because I want the QR monster generation features to be fully accessible across PC and consoles, i want to make sure every single player has the exact same access to discovery—whether you have a webcam or not.

Here is how you will find and summon monsters, no matter how you play:

1. The QR Code Scanner (For Mobile & Webcam Users)  
Described already. A cool way to discover for those that choose to use it.

2. The "DNA Signature" Input (For Console, PC & Camera-free Players)  
Don't have a webcam? Don't want to use a mobile app? You can use a  fully integrated system that lets you tap into the exact same mechanics without needing any external hardware.  
Every single monster in the game generates a unique number - a DNA Signature (the seed number).  
When a player scans a QR code and posts their cool new monster online, the monster’s display panel in the game will clearly show its seed number.  
All you have to do is enter that number into the Qreature Lab and generate the exact same monster with the exact same stats. You can freely collect, replicate, and share any community discovery!

3. The Text Input (For the experimenters)  
Type literally anything into the system. It could be your name, your dog’s name, a random phrase, or even a website URL.  
The game hashes your text into a unique DNA Signature to spawn a monster. The words you use have permanent power—if you type the exact same word again (or give it to a friend to type), it will always generate that exact same monster.

The Bottom Line: Multiple Paths, Same Results  
I designed this system so nobody gets left behind. QR scanners get the fun of exploring the real world, text-explorers get the fun of hunting for secret word combinations, and console/camera-free players get full access to the global network of community discoveries via DNA Signatures.

Word phrases can be shared.  
Seed numbers can be shared.  
Qr codes can be shared.  
They are all just containers for the same mechanic that points to infinite monsters to discover.

Breeding ANY two monsters remains the same as this doesn’t require scanning. Same for Evolving any monster.

Your feedback in this Reddit thread is what helped me to come up with these solutions. Thank you all!
